newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat to softer, retail perks up.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat to softer, retail perks up.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were pegged from flat to slightly softer in late trade on Tuesday, as dealers smiled at brisk orders placed by retail investors for New York City's and the University of Connecticut's bonds.
"I'm impressed with all the retail that's getting done," a trader said. "We haven't seen that in awhile."
New York City sold $304 million of tax-exempt bonds to retail investors during a pre-sale period that ended at midday, its third biggest showing.

On Wednesday, the city is selling $900 million of tax-exempt bonds through a syndicate led by Smith Barney, $120 million of taxable bonds through competition, and about $50 million of taxable bonds that are earmarked for European investors.
The strong demand seen during New York City's retail presale period, which ended at midday on Tuesday, enabled the city to close out six maturities, from 1999 to 2004.

There was speculation that the $120 million sale by the University of Connecticut might have drawn enough retail interest during its retail presale period, which also ended on Tuesday, to close out more maturities.
"That deal, everything through 2010 is done retail, which is more than half of the loan," a trader said.
A spokeswoman for A.G. Edwards & Sons, which is leading the syndicate, said that unofficial results showed that it was able to close at least seven maturities.
"The deal went very well with strong acceptance by retail," said Margaret Welch, a spokeswoman.

Traders also pointed to Massachusetts Water Pollution Trust's $138 million deal, which was repriced by lowering yields in the 1999 maturity by 10 basis points to 4.30 percent, and the 2000 maturity by five basis points to 4.55 percent.

Further evidence of the market's healthy appetite for new issues was seen in Georgia's sale of $307 million of general obligation bonds, which had only a $47 million balance left at 1245 EDT. The bonds were awarded to Goldman Sachs with a 5.277 percent net interest cost shortly after 1100 EST.

And Puerto Rico's Finance Agency's sale of $277 million of bonds were repriced, with the top yield cut two basis points to 5.83 percent, along with other adjustments. To see the story, double click on N0814276.
The island also sold $148 million of general obligation bonds that were priced with a top yield of 4.90 percent in 2003.

The secondary market, however, was lackluster, with prices seen from unchanged to down about an eighth of a point, as the market was unable to resist the downward pressure exerted by lower Treasury bonds.
Sikeston, Mo., electricity revenue refundings of June 2022, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.90 percent, up one basis point.
And Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of January 2026, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.87 percent, up two basis points.
In futures markets, the June municipal contracts fell five ticks to 111-30/32. The June Treasury bond contracts slipped seven ticks to 107-13/32. The MOB spread was at 145 ticks.
